sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: Italian arum is a tuberous perennial native from Macaronesia and western Europe to Iraq. Its arrow-shaped leaves can reach about 40 × 29 cm and have pale veins; the leaf stalk is up to roughly 40 cm. A pale spathe encloses the spadix, and the mature red-berry spike can reach about 12 cm.

sections.title: Toxicity
sections.text: All parts of Arum contain irritating calcium-oxalate crystals and can cause poisoning. No edible part is described. The plate's patterned leaves, pale spathe and red berries are consistent with the species.
